title: Mouse Tower
visualBrief: Specific current Mouse Tower at Bingen: mapped asymmetric main body/projecting eastern stair turret, pale plaster/stone corner pilasters and bands, small genuinely recessed closed windows, projecting corbel gallery/flat deck and open crenellated parapet, taller octagonal shaft/lancet head/closed cap and crenellated crown, sparse iron rods, bounded dark lower housing/hip cap. Four existing shared stucco/raw sandstone/slate/paint graphs. No older red finish, copied heraldry/inscriptions/photo atlas, furnished interior, neighboring castle, whole island mesh or river-covering platform.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Retained exact-QID OSMway50828644/native named building35184422917476 identify the tower. Own anchor7.880397636,49.972056547, global heading0/native east-south; body quadrilateral provides internal X/Z axes and centre[-0.9476146934689381,-0.05791476925351979]m. Eastward mapped footprint projection fixes the stair turret side and agrees with ordinary river-side pictures. Main body roughly6.830x7.702m; full asymmetric outline is retained. Fine facade/window/housing allocation retains20degree/2m approximation; the offset older reference point does not control placement.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Retained map has four building levels and one roof level but no qualified height. Native PMTiles supplies an unqualified14m value, compatible with a level-derived generic body estimate rather than a measurement of the taller head. Picture-led visualization uses main body/corbel13.4..14m, gallery/roof deck17.2m, main crenels18.5m, projecting shaft19.2m, lancet head23.8m/cap24m and crown25m, with sparse iron rods to25.6m. Dimensions/closed-window/reverse/corbel/upper opening inventory and lower housing2.6m cap are explicit estimates, not a conservation survey.
